old:
A three-workflow GitHub Actions pipeline covers the full delivery lifecycle: 
 1. lint.yml (syntax, style, types on every push), 
 2. test.yaml (matrix unit tests plus per-PR agent evaluation), and 
 3. publish.yml (PyPI release triggered on a new GitHub release tag). [q-71]

They scaled their infrastructure in 2 patterns - 
 Pattern 1: Single backend with agent loop and isolated terminal uses a sandbox for tool-calling via HTTP.
 Pattern 2: Isolate the agent. The entire agent runs in a sandbox with zero secrets. It talks to the outside world through a control plane that holds all the credentials. [q-74] [q-116]

They switched from pattern 1 to 2 for scalability, decoupling, and security. [q-74] [q-116] [q-117]

The tradeoff is an extra network hop (control plane) on every operation and three services to deploy instead of one.
 In practice, the latency is noise compared to LLM response times, and the operational complexity is the kind that ops teams already know how to handle. [q-118]

Their cloud service receives task requests, sends them to an SQS (Amazon's Queue Service) queue, and returns an HTTP 202 response. 
 A Lambda worker (serverless process runner) then processes each queued task and runs the agent until completion. [q-72]

In July 2026 the agent sandboxes moved onto AWS Bedrock AgentCore, which provisions a per-session micro-VM and is managed in Terraform; the zero-secret sandbox and the control plane (on ECS Fargate) were kept. [q-123]

Mobile-Agent (v3) is an open-source, cross-platform GUI automation agent developed by Tongyi Lab at Alibaba Group. Its core is GUI-Owl — a foundational vision-language model built on Qwen2.5-VL, wrapped in a four-role multi-agent framework (Manager, Worker, Reflector, Notetaker) that automates tasks on Android phones, PCs, and web browsers without requiring app-specific training. [q-1]

old:
The team evaluates GUI-Owl across ten public benchmarks covering grounding, single-step decision, question answering, and online interactive task completion. Benchmarks include ScreenSpot-v2, ScreenSpot-Pro, OSWorld-Verified, etc. [q-3] [q-67]

Agent behaviour is validated by running the full agent stack against AndroidWorld and OSWorld interactive environments. They launch live agent sessions against real or emulated devices and measure end-to-end task success rate. [q-3]

The team relies on issue reports to detect runtime failures that would otherwise require live device testing. [q-4]
